comparator.sourceNotes: The 2025–2026 regulations, Appendix 1 and Articles 3.15, 4.2 and 5.3, establish the illustrated route. Each of the first two years has twelve 4 EC courses and two 6 EC projects. Year 2 includes one Period 5 elective. Year 3 has six 4 EC electives, a 6 EC project, three 4 EC core courses and an 18 EC thesis. A student who passes each year on schedule meets project and examination progression requirements. The thesis requires at least 138 EC overall, including 60 EC from Year 1 and at least 40 EC from Year 2. The current programme overview corroborates the broad structure. The component list is specific to the published 2025–2026 regulations.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Three plans develop the main technical core, medical applications, and cognition, language and philosophy. Each pair differs by at least four courses and has a distinct academic progression. Robotics contributes manipulation and motion planning, but a separate robotics option would largely duplicate the cognition and AI spine without a sustained embedded-systems or control sequence. Planning and optimisation contribute to logistics, but the available courses do not sustain a distinct supply-chain, operations or simulation sequence. Mathematical coursework supports subject knowledge for teaching, but there is no corresponding school-based teaching and subject-didactics pathway.
